label: Star Filter
blurb: The glass star filter a camera screws on the front of the lens: every small bright thing in the shot grows a set of straight rays running out of it, so street lamps, candles, speculars on water and highlights on chrome all turn into stars. Choose four, six or eight points, turn the whole set to any angle, and set how far the rays reach and how fast they fall off. The rays can split into colour along their length the way real ruled glass does, and only the parts of the picture above the brightness you set make them, so the rest of the shot is untouched.
